dossier.public_summary: The 13-day dip looks like a shallow 1.2-Earth-radius transit but is not stable. Its depth jumps from zero to over 1000 ppm between sectors and individual transits, with nearly all the signal coming from just three strong outliers. With an inconclusive centroid and two nearby stars that could mimic this depth, the best explanation is a blend or systematic false alarm rather than a planet.

reasons.why: Depth is not constant across sectors (chi2 225.1 dof 9); per-sector depths range from -70 ppm to 1028 ppm with 3 sectors at zero and 2 at ~1000 ppm. Alone not enough, but combined with other variability it favors non-planet.

Individual transits are wildly inconsistent; signal is dominated by 3 outliers (depths 2292, 1068, 982 ppm vs mean 229 ppm, sigma 15.1, 11.7, 9.9). This is the signature of a few blended/ systematics events, not a repeated planet transit.
The depth change is real, not a cross-catalogue calibration offset: it changes within SPOC 2-min and within TESS-SPOC, as seen above.

Cannot localize with difference imaging, plus 2 neighbours plausible_within_1px that could cause depth with eclipse_needed 0.0458 at 8.7 arcsec and 0.0057 at 21 arcsec, so a blended NEB remains viable and positively favors blend over on-target planet.
reasons.value: inconclusive, centroid_all inconclusive why no sector with a clear difference image

reasons.why: Independent scorer rates this as planet-like as only the lowest 6% of known planets, supporting the variability and blend picture over a planet.
